body.statement: For a nonzero contrast matrix \(C\), the positive-semidefinite dominance \[\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}\succeq\Sigma_C(Y)\quad\text{for every }N\text{ divisible by }2K,F,\text{ and }Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)\] holds if and only if all columns of \(C\) vanish except two columns that are negatives of one another. Equivalently, every nonzero universally Loewner-dominated multi-contrast system is a vector rescaling of one pairwise arm contrast. For any other \(C\), there is a direction \(h\) and binary armwise marginals for which common ranking reduces \(\operatorname{Var}_Z(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau)\).
body.justification: Scalar risk optimality does not imply joint covariance conservativeness; this theorem identifies the exact and unexpectedly narrow boundary.
body.gap: No located causal-bootstrap or multi-arm design paper classifies when one completed science table dominates the full covariance matrix for all marginal schedules.
body.consumer: Analysts constructing simultaneous Wald regions learn when a single rank-preserving bootstrap covariance is valid and when contrast-specific completion is unavoidable.
body.proof_tex:
For a fixed completion pair, a symmetric matrix difference is positive semidefinite exactly when all its quadratic forms are nonnegative.  Thus the asserted universal Loewner dominance is equivalent to
\[
 h^{\mathsf T}\!\left[\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\Sigma_C(Y)\right]h\geq0
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\mathbb R^m,F,Y.
\]
For a given \(h\), put \(c=C^{\mathsf T}h\).  The displayed quadratic form is the scalarized covariance difference for the one-row contrast \(c^{\mathsf T}\) and scalar weight one.  Since \(c^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_K=h^{\mathsf T}C\mathbf 1_K=0\), \(\texttt{thm:rank-cone-iff}\) applies and says that this scalar inequality holds universally exactly when
\[
 cc^{\mathsf T}\in\mathcal R_K,
 \quad\text{equivalently}\quad
 c_ac_b\leq0\quad(a\ne b).
\]
Therefore universal Loewner dominance is equivalent to the following property of the linear space \(L=\operatorname{range}(C^{\mathsf T})\): every \(c\in L\) has pairwise nonpositive distinct-coordinate products.

We now characterize such a space.  Every nonzero \(c\in L\) has coordinate sum zero.  It therefore has a positive and a negative coordinate.  Pairwise nonpositive products prohibit two positive coordinates and also prohibit two negative coordinates.  Hence every nonzero \(c\in L\) has exactly two nonzero coordinates and is of the form \(t(e_p-e_q)\).  Fix one such vector.  If another vector in \(L\) used a different coordinate pair, then a generic nonzero linear combination of the two vectors (choose the scalar outside the finitely many values causing coordinate cancellation) would have at least three nonzero coordinates, contradicting the preceding conclusion.  It follows that
\[
 L\subseteq\operatorname{span}(e_p-e_q)
\]
for one fixed pair \(p\ne q\).  Equivalently, all columns of \(C\) except columns \(p,q\) vanish and \(C_{\cdot q}=-C_{\cdot p}\).  Because \(C\ne0\), this is a nonzero vector rescaling of the pairwise contrast.  Conversely, this column form makes every \(C^{\mathsf T}h\) a multiple of \(e_p-e_q\), so every matrix \(cc^{\mathsf T}\) lies in \(\mathcal R_K\), proving Loewner dominance.

If \(C\) does not have this form, the characterization supplies an \(h\) and distinct arms \(a,b\) with \(c_ac_b>0\).  The binary construction in the necessity part of \(\texttt{thm:rank-cone-iff}\), applied to \(cc^{\mathsf T}\), then gives
\[
 h^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}h
 <h^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_C(Y)h.
\]
This is precisely the claimed binary witness that common ranking reduces the randomization variance in direction \(h\).
